title: Broccoli Stem and Gruyère Cream
description: Peeled fresh broccoli stems give this smooth Gruyère sauce a mild sweetness and a use for the tender centers of the stalks.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: peeled fresh broccoli stems
ingredients.note: Weigh after removing the woody outer layer. Cut into thin coins.

steps.title: Soften the broccoli stems
steps.text: Put {stems}, {mustard} and {broth} in the HexClad. Cover and simmer for 9–13 minutes until a coin mashes under a spoon.

steps.title: Make the stem puree
steps.text: Blend the stems and broth with {milk} in a deep jug until smooth. Press through a fine sieve into the skillet to remove any tough fibers.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Set the reduction
steps.text: Measure the base and return it to the skillet. Aim for about 1 3/8 cups. If needed, simmer briefly to reduce or add a splash of water to reach the mark.

steps.title: Melt the Gruyère
steps.text: Take the skillet off heat and add {gruyere} gradually, whisking until each addition melts.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon around pieces of chicken or over a baked potato split and mashed with its sauce.

notes: Yield: 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: Peel and slice the broccoli stems a day ahead and refrigerate covered. Finely grate the cheese shortly before cooking. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Fully finished Gruyère sauce can turn grainy after thawing. For freezer prep, keep the blended stem base for up to 2 months and add the cheese after reheating. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion over medium-low heat, whisking to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Whisk off heat until smooth. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. For dairy-free sauce, use plain unsweetened oat milk and a smooth mild dairy-free cheese that melts. For a gentler flavor, leave out the ground mustard. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 42 kcal, 3.1 g protein, 3.7 g total carbohydrate, 1.6 g fat, 0.5 g fiber, 57 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal. Fiber is estimated before straining.
